authority_boundary: This richer DAD card catalog advertises assets, skills, templates, harnesses, architecture references, maps, and known upgrades as candidate offerings. Target repos decide local adoption.

offerings.name: AI Engineering Preflight
applies_when: An AI agent is about to perform material software work.
does_not_apply_when: The task is a read-only lookup or the target repo has not approved DAD pointers.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own this card; the target repository owner controls adoption.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate pointer only; adoption requires explicit local review and a recorded local decision.
offerings.authority_boundary: Candidate reusable engineering guidance; local tests and repo authority decide adoption.

offerings.name: Agent Skill Library
applies_when: A repo needs to know which agent skills to use without copying full skill bodies.
does_not_apply_when: A full skill install or plugin install is requested without explicit local approval.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own this card; the target repository owner controls skill checkout.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Pointer only; checkout requires an explicit target-repository decision and does not copy a skill automatically.
offerings.authority_boundary: Skill records are pointers and lifecycle metadata; target repos decide checkout.

offerings.name: Python Underused Idioms AI Coding Card
applies_when: An AI agent is writing, refactoring, reviewing, debugging, or researching Python code and should consider under-represented stdlib constructs.
A review wants citable idiom ids for suggested improvements.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo's Python floor is below an idiom's min_python.
Working code would be rewritten solely to use an idiom without a task-level reason.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own this card; the target repository owner controls style and adoption.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate guidance only; each idiom requires local applicability review and task-relevant tests.
offerings.authority_boundary: Idioms are candidate guidance gated by avoid_when conditions; local repo style authority wins on conflict.

offerings.name: Rust Buildout And Python-To-Rust Migration Guide
applies_when: A task mentions performance, Rust, ports, parsing speed, or replacing a profiled Python hot path.
A repo is deciding whether Rust pays off before writing any Rust.
does_not_apply_when: No profile evidence exists yet (stage 1 requires profiling first).
The work is I/O-bound glue or a fast-changing prototype.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own this card; the target repository owner and human Rust gate control adoption.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate planning guidance only; profiling, shadow parity, and a separate human gate are required before Rust expansion.
offerings.authority_boundary: Stage gates (profile evidence, parity reports, human review for full ports) are the enforceable part; language preference is not.

offerings.name: DAD Rust Scan Core And Rollout Control Plane
applies_when: DAD needs deterministic local source observations or hash manifests.
An agent is validating DAD's first Rust leaf tool.
A repo needs Rust rollout packets, target ownership rules, or Logos instruction-only boundaries.
Multiple repos are sending Rust rollout feedback and DAD must distinguish source outbox traffic from central collection/routing/delivery audit.
does_not_apply_when: The task needs governance meaning, final asset value scoring, legal judgment, theological judgment, or model orchestration.
A downstream repo lacks a reviewed local path or is Logos instruction-mail-only.
Rust output would be treated as canonical source truth instead of candidate evidence.
A clean Rust mail-spool probe is being used as all-repo delivery approval instead of running mail doctor with reviewed repo coverage.

known_upgrades.summary: Initial DAD-local Rust scan core, Python bridge, rollout policy, local instruction packets, and lesson ledger.

offerings.owner_authority: DAD owns the experimental leaf contract; Python policy and the target repository owner retain final authority.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Internal experimental leaf only; no downstream rollout, replacement, or promotion follows from catalog matching.
offerings.authority_boundary: Rust emits candidate observations only. Python/DAD retains orchestration and review authority; downstream apply is policy gated and Logos repos are instruction-mail-only. Rust rollout feedback originates in source repo outboxes; DAD central inbox/outbox rows require collection and route audit.

offerings.name: Rust Shadow Parity Harness
applies_when: A repo is considering Rust replacement or shadow tests for a slow Python test battery.
does_not_apply_when: The Rust suite does not have structured coverage evidence matching Python tests.

known_upgrades.summary: Initial candidate harness for Python/Rust test parity timing and audit.

offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own this harness card; the target repository owner controls any experiment.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate harness only; a match may propose a shadow test but cannot authorize Rust promotion.
offerings.authority_boundary: Rust timing claims are gated behind verified structured parity.

offerings.name: Python Test Performance And Orchestration Harness
applies_when: A Python repo's full test battery is too slow or poorly targeted.
does_not_apply_when: Skipping tests would hide coverage for a risky shared behavior change.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own this harness card; the target repository owner controls test strategy.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate test plan only; selected tests never replace required local validation.
offerings.authority_boundary: Test selection is a proposal; full validation remains required for risky changes.

offerings.name: Repo Enrollment Mail Governance Safety Harness
applies_when: DAD is planning or applying enrollment, mail delivery, Rust rollout packets, or governance updates.
Multiple repos or branches are sending DAD mail and the worktree looks very dirty.
does_not_apply_when: A repo is not in reviewed policy or lacks a human approval ID for broad writes.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD governance owns this safety contract; each target repository owner controls enrollment and mail adoption.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate safety route only; enrollment, delivery, public release, and rollout each retain their separate gates.
offerings.authority_boundary: Normal recurring DAD operation writes only mailbox files; broader changes require approval.

offerings.name: Exception Capture Completeness Harness
applies_when: A repo should prove it would emit DAD-worthy mail, exception, fix, usage, or no packet without Lowell rescuing the miss from chat.
DAD changes wanted asset, harness, skill, template, workflow, governance, data-map, mail, exception, review, fix, or learning-loop patterns.
A pattern update adds required metadata fields that enrolled repos must emit, not just recognize.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo has not approved DAD pointers or enrollment refresh checks.
The evidence requires raw logs, private rows, secrets, or copied source blobs instead of pointer-safe metadata.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD governance owns this harness card; source repositories retain authority over their observations.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate evaluation only; passing scenarios do not promote rules or establish source truth.
offerings.authority_boundary: Capture-completeness results are candidate evidence; they prove scenario coverage and observed outbox comparisons, not source truth or public safety.

offerings.name: Exception Learning Readiness Harness
applies_when: DAD changes exception learning queue statuses, blockers, fix-outcome validation, public/private release gates, or backfill promotion boundaries.
A future agent wants proof that exception clusters do not become learnable from weak or mixed evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The question is whether a repo emitted a packet at all; use the exception capture completeness harness instead.
The evidence requires raw logs, private rows, secrets, or copied source blobs instead of pointer-safe metadata.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD governance owns this harness card; humans retain lesson-promotion authority.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate evaluation only; synthetic readiness cannot promote a lesson or learning rule.
offerings.authority_boundary: Learning-readiness results are synthetic candidate evidence; they do not promote lessons, prove real repo completeness, or override source authority.

offerings.name: Harness Vs Deterministic Enforcement Decision Model
applies_when: An agent discovers an issue, pattern, review finding, or coding improvement and must decide whether it belongs in a harness, advisory report, warning, or deterministic gate.
A repo is accumulating too many hard checks and needs to separate learning surfaces from non-negotiable safety boundaries.
A finding has uneven risk across public-safe, internal, confidential, protected, or public-release contexts.
does_not_apply_when: A non-negotiable security, privacy, public-release, source-authority, or human-approval gate already clearly requires deterministic enforcement.
The task is a trivial local edit with no repeated pattern, no learning value, and no downstream consumer.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD governance owns this decision guide; the target repository owner selects enforcement.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Advisory decision support only; no harness or deterministic control is installed automatically.
offerings.authority_boundary: Advisory routing only. It does not override local repo authority, required validation, human gates, public/private release gates, or source-of-truth rules.

offerings.name: Claude Architectural Root-Cause Review Packets
applies_when: A repo sees repeated integration failures, implementation drift, boundary mismatch, ownership ambiguity, sequencing errors, or review findings that may have an architectural root cause.
A coding agent wants Claude to analyze root cause from safe metadata instead of raw logs, private rows, copied source, or chat transcripts.
does_not_apply_when: The issue is a trivial isolated local typo or obvious one-command fix with no repeated pattern, boundary concern, or learning value.
The packet would require copying secrets, raw logs, stack traces, private rows, full source files, hidden reasoning, or raw review transcripts.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD architecture owns the packet format; the DAD boss architect and human retain decisions.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Exceptional-review route only; a returned review remains candidate evidence and cannot approve implementation.
offerings.authority_boundary: Claude review packets are candidate analysis requests. They do not approve fixes, override local source authority, or bypass human gates.

offerings.name: Language Coding Advantage Registry
applies_when: A coding agent needs Python, Rust, or future-language guidance before implementation.
A repo discovers a language technique, library, crate, tool, or validation idea that might improve AI coding.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo's local language authority conflicts with the suggestion.
The evidence is only a benchmark, blog claim, or agent preference with no local validation idea.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own this card; the target repository owner controls language choices.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate guidance only; matching never selects a language or authorizes code changes.
offerings.authority_boundary: Candidate language guidance only; local repo authority, validation, security policy, and human gates decide adoption.

offerings.name: Language Coding Playbooks
applies_when: An agent is about to write Python, Rust, mixed-language, or new-language code.
A repo or agent needs the short operational rules before consulting the full language registry.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo's local language authority conflicts with the playbook.
The agent wants to promote a frontier technique without local validation and postflight evidence.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD catalog maintainers own these pointers; the target repository owner controls playbook use.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate playbook only; local validation and security review precede any application.
offerings.authority_boundary: Candidate language playbooks only; repo-local authority, validation, security policy, and human gates decide adoption.

offerings.name: Language Frontier Research Harness
applies_when: A repo or agent finds a Python, Rust, mixed-language, or future-language technique that may improve AI coding.
DAD needs to decide whether a frontier language signal belongs in an idiom card, buildout guide, coding tactic, or harness eval.
does_not_apply_when: The evidence is copied third-party docs, copied source, private rows, raw logs, credentials, or benchmark-only claims.
No proof surface, validation command, or applicability limit can be named.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD research governance owns this harness card; target repositories retain adoption authority.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Pointer-only candidate research; no external code, dependency, or recommendation is adopted automatically.
offerings.authority_boundary: The harness routes language-frontier ideas as candidate evidence only; target repos retain local authority and must validate before adoption.

offerings.name: DAD 9-Layer Learning Address Model
applies_when: A repo needs to log digital assets without copying private source content.
DAD needs to connect prior fixes, derivative solutions, validation deltas, and future lookup triggers.
A workflow or orchestration asset needs compact representation through refs instead of copied long prose.
An architecture or learning-loop change needs stable address placement alongside graph edges.
does_not_apply_when: The task is a tiny one-off change with no future-agent reuse value.
The model would add ceremony without improving identity, retrieval, validation, provenance, or learning.
A source repo has stronger local address authority and DAD is only collecting pointer metadata.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD architecture owns the address vocabulary; source systems retain record authority.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate coordinate model only; use requires explicit local mapping and does not create graph truth.
offerings.authority_boundary: DAD address-model guidance is a compact coordinate system for candidate records. It does not replace graph edges, prove truth or value, import LawFirm OS canon, or authorize source mutation.

offerings.name: Machine Learning Workflow Agent Family
applies_when: A repo needs to decide whether ML fits an end goal or to execute a governed ML workflow.
A reusable ML role, technique, runtime binding, harness, or dependency needs lifecycle review.
does_not_apply_when: A deterministic or ordinary statistical solution fully meets the goal with lower risk and cost.
The requested action would bypass data, domain, privacy, safety, deployment, automation, or human authority.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD owns the candidate family and registry metadata; source repositories and named humans own ML data, domain, deployment, and adoption decisions.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Pointer or lightweight wrapper only; checkout and live global installation require an explicit local decision and do not activate research automation.
offerings.authority_boundary: This offering routes and governs candidate ML work; it cannot authorize data access, model training, deployment, recurring research, instruction changes, or supersession.

offerings.name: Agent-Family Portfolio Control Plane
applies_when: A material request may need one or more governed reusable capability families, independent assurance, or lifecycle monitoring.
does_not_apply_when: A narrower deterministic tool or existing DAD skill completes the request without a family mesh.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD owns portfolio metadata and projections; each source repository and named human owns adoption, code, policy, release, legal, and external-system decisions.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Read-only routing and inspection by default; skill checkout remains pointer or wrapper based and no recurring routine is activated.
offerings.authority_boundary: The control plane proposes family combinations, graph evidence, health issues, pilots, and at most three cockpit decisions. It cannot dispatch, mutate, promote, release, or make legal conclusions.

offerings.name: Technical Product Company Operating System
applies_when: A technical product request needs to be shaped, routed, governed, coordinated, measured, or improved without losing reusable capability knowledge.
does_not_apply_when: A single deterministic command or narrower existing skill completes the request without material routing, authority, or lifecycle judgment.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD owns candidate catalog, routing, receipts, and projections; source repositories and the named human retain project truth, adoption, activation, code, policy, release, spend, legal, data, and external-system authority.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Candidate and read-only by default. Telemetry is explicit opt-in, routines require separate activation, and adapters require exact configuration and permission.
offerings.authority_boundary: The OS can observe, retrieve, recommend, draft, and independently validate inside declared bounds. It cannot grant execution, activate itself, approve its own outputs, or perform prohibited actions.

offerings.name: Knowledge Engineering Ops
applies_when: A repo needs a governed knowledge, retrieval, context, vector, or graph system.
An existing RAG, chunker, embedding, index, graph, or vector database needs evaluation, migration, or lifecycle review.
does_not_apply_when: A direct deterministic source query fully meets the bounded goal.
The requested action would bypass source, privacy, provider, infrastructure, deployment, schedule, or human authority.
offerings.owner_authority: DAD owns candidate skill, registry, and graph metadata; source repositories and named humans own corpus, domain, privacy, provider, infrastructure, adoption, release, schedule, cutover, and retirement decisions.
offerings.adoption_semantics: Pointer or wrapper by default; the explicitly requested personal global copy remains separately runtime-authoritative and does not activate weekly research or downstream adoption.
offerings.authority_boundary: This offering can diagnose, design, implement in approved scope, and independently validate; it cannot access new corpora, activate recurring research, install infrastructure, deploy, or self-approve.
